item.title: Silicon Valley Is Still Defending Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia employees and tech insiders never thought the chip king would lose his job. Despite his sudden resignation, many of them are still in denial.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is Out. Will Nvidia’s Rivals Cash In?
item.description: In a special episode of “Uncanny Valley,” we break down Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia, what comes next for the company, and where the AI industry goes from here.

item.title: Jensen Huang Didn’t Name His Own Replacement as One of Tech’s Most Powerful Women
item.description: A recent WIRED investigation explored the complicated definition of “power” for women in the industry. Jensen Huang’s answers now appear to show his blind spots.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s $470 Billion Affair
item.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” the team unpacks the Nvidia CEO’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy and what that means for the AI industry.

item.title: Google DeepMind Staff Tap the UK Government to Escalate Their Unionization Fight
item.description: After initial talks stalled, workers at Google DeepMind are trying to bypass company management in their bid to unionize.

item.title: Jensen Huang Basically Lit More Than $1 Trillion on Fire in Less Than a Month
item.description: Since the scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy began, Nvidia has lost an eye-watering sum from its market value.

item.title: Meet Colette Kress, Nvidia’s New Interim CEO
item.description: Nvidia’s longtime chief financial officer helped transform the company into an AI powerhouse. Now she’s taking the reins following Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday.

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Nvidia’s cofounder and chief executive resigned on Thursday after the company opened an investigation into his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.

item.title: Alex Karp Said He’s a ‘Progressive.’ OK! Here’s Some Other Stuff He’s Said Recently
item.description: The Palantir CEO touted his “progressive” worldview in a recent interview. Let’s see how that lines up with his comments during the company’s earnings call two weeks ago.

item.title: Google Wanted Spirit Airlines Data. Flight Attendants Found a Way to Opt Out
item.description: The union representing flight attendants for the defunct airline struck a deal with Google to scrub sensitive employee records from a $10 million data sale.
